title: Simon's Algorithm
summary: Recover a hidden XOR mask from outcomes that are orthogonal to it.
objectives: Say what each measurement of Simon's circuit tells you about s
Collect outcomes and solve y·s = 0 (mod 2) to find the hidden string
Explain why n − 1 independent outcomes fix s, and how s = 000 shows up
mission: Find the hidden mask s of a function f from 3 bits to 3 bits with f(x) = f(y) if and only if y = x or y = x ⊕ s (s may be 000, when f is one-to-one). Call oracle(qc) once (input register: qubits 0 to 2, output register: qubits 3 to 5), measure the input register into bits 0 to 2, and collect outcomes with run_shots. Then compute from the outcomes alone the bit string s_found equal to s. Qubit 0 is the last character of every string, so s = s2 s1 s0 and an outcome is y2 y1 y0.

prediction.question: For n = 3 you have measured y = 011 and y = 101. A third run gives 110. How much does it add?
options: Nothing new: 110 = 011 ⊕ 101, so it is not an independent equation
A third independent equation, which fixes s
Nothing new: it repeats one of the earlier outcomes
prediction.explanation: Adding 011 and 101 bit by bit gives 110, so the equation for 110 follows from the other two and cuts nothing off. Only independent outcomes reduce the solution space, and here two already left a single nonzero s. The third outcome is not a repeat of an earlier string either.

hints: Put Hadamard gates on qubits 0 to 2 before and after oracle(qc) and leave qubits 3 to 5 alone. Then measure qubits 0 to 2 and call run_shots.
Each key of counts is a y with y·s = 0 (mod 2). For two bit strings a and b, bin(int(a, 2) & int(b, 2)).count("1") % 2 is the inner product.
Which of the nonzero strings "001" to "111" have inner product 0 with every key? If one is left, it is s. If none is left, f is one-to-one and s is "000".

challenge.mission: Simon's problem with a compact oracle. The function f takes 3 bits to 2 bits and satisfies f(x) = f(y) if and only if y = x or y = x ⊕ s, for a hidden nonzero string s (never 000: with 2 output bits, f cannot be one-to-one on 8 inputs). Use a circuit qc with 5 qubits (input register: qubits 0 to 2, output register: qubits 3 and 4) and 3 classical bits, call oracle(qc) once, measure the input register into bits 0 to 2, and store in s_found the string s computed from the outcomes. Qubit 0 is the last character of every string.
hints: How many output qubits does this function need? Count the output bits.
The procedure is the same as in the lesson: Hadamard gates, one query, Hadamard gates, measure qubits 0 to 2.
With a nonzero s the outcomes span a 2-dimensional space, so exactly one nonzero string is orthogonal to all of them.
